incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Hosted API p99 latency > 12s and request queue growing for us-east-1 (gpu-serving). Auto-scaler reports repeated allocation failures. Paging #incidents and infra-oncall. root_ts=7321112223

infra-oncall: I'm on it, grabbing metrics now. seeing backlog ~11.8k requests, queue-increase-rate ~2.3k/min. p95 ~1.4s, p99 ~13.6s.

dylan: that backlog is massive. any customer-visible 504s?

support-ryan: yes, we've got multiple customer reports of timeouts for text-generation endpoints. Support triage: high-impact customers affected in prod.

jules: quick snapshot from the autoscaler: "AllocationError: quotaExceeded" when trying to spin new gpu nodes. Cloud console shows per-project gpu quota at limit.

samir: confirmed. autoscaler loop: tried 4 times in last 6 minutes, each attempt failed with 403 quota error. Logs: ```2026-03-15T04:12:10Z autoscaler: request new-gpu-pool size=6 -> error: QuotaExceeded(project=redwood-prod, resource=GPU, limit=120, used=120)```

alexa: any existing warm pools we can pinch? maybe reduce batch sizes or move heavy tenants to a limited fallback?

maria: we have a small reserve pool (gpu-reserve-1) but it's currently at capacity serving dedicated customers. Can't evict them.

jules: two parallel mitigations we should run now: 1) apply immediate tenant-level rate limits for the top 5 noisy tenants; 2) enable fallback routing for low-tier traffic to CPU-run smaller models to reduce GPU pressure.

infra-oncall: I'm going to push a soft throttle rule for tenant selectors: ```/api/v1/generate tenant in (tenantA,tenantB,tenantC) -> rate_limit=30rps``` Applying now.

incident-bot: action recorded: soft-throttle applied by infra-oncall.

support-ryan: FYI notified impacted SOC contacts for tenantA and tenantB. We're sending status emails and keeping them updated.

samir: enabling baseline fallback routing: route matches (tier=free OR route contains "/quick-") -> model=cpu-small-v1, timeout=6s. Pushing as a temporary policy.

dylan: behind the firewall, can we also reduce default token window or limit max tokens to cut GPU time per request?

alexa: yes, pushing a global max_tokens cap from 1024 -> 512 for hosted-default route. Doing a rolling change with 10s TTL on the config so we can revert fast.

jules: also request cache: turn on aggressive prefix caching for identical prompt patterns from large customers (cache TTL 60s). Could save ~20% of tokens if hit-rate improves.

infra-oncall: Cache rule in place. Initial metrics show cache-hit ~8% -> need 30% for meaningful relief. We'll watch.

samir: for visibility: queue length before mitigations 11.8k. After throttles/fallbacks applied 5 min ago, current queue=6.2k. p99 trending down to 9.1s but still high.

maria: good progress. but autoscaler errors remain because cloud quota is saturated — need quota increase from cloud provider or manual reallocation.

dylan: can we temporarily borrow GPUs from Dedicated pools (internal-multiprod) and mark them as preemptible for hosted? Risky but could save customers.

jules: Legal/contract concerns for dedicated customers. However infra team, any spare nodes in less critical regions we can cold-migrate?

infra-oncall: scanning pools... found 8 spare GPUs in eu-west-2 low-priority cluster. Cross-region failover would add 120-250ms to latency for those routed customers. We can create a fast-failover policy: route select tenants to eu-west-2 if they opt-in. Not ideal for all.

support-ryan: push opt-in notices? That will be messy but doable for specific customers. For now I'd prefer noise-targeted throttles and fallback.

incident-bot: incident severity bumped to P1. Pager duty escalations sent to oncall.

samir: also saw a secondary problem: the autoscaler controller is hitting API rate limits when provisioning many small pulls quickly — we might be triggering provider-side throttle causing some allocation failures to surface as quota errors. Working on backoff tuning.

alexa: action checklist: 1) maintain tenant soft-throttles (infra-oncall) 2) keep fallback routing active (samir) 3) reduce default max_tokens (alexa) 4) request emergency quota increase from cloud (maria) 5) consider manual cross-pool borroW (dylan/jules).

infra-oncall: continuing monitoring. queue=3.9k now, p99=6.8s, p95=1.2s. Noticed a spike in one route: /v1/chat/generate?model=bigchat-2 is 65% of incoming tokens.

jules: can we hot-swap that route to a trimmed variant `bigchat-2-compact` that uses fewer layers / quantized weights? That would reduce per-token GPU time by ~30%.

samir: we have a compatible variant available in the model catalog. Initiating immediate route-model-swap for that route for non-SLA tenants. Command: ```route manager swap-model --route "*/chat/generate" --from bigchat-2 --to bigchat-2-compact --selector "tenant not in (enterpriseX,enterpriseY)"```

incident-bot: route change executed by samir. Change id=chg-20260315-001.

maria: status on quota request: raised emergency ticket with cloud provider 18m ago, they're queueing. No immediate ETA.

dylan: what about progressive request draining? Could we reject excessively long prompts at the edge with 429 and instruct clients to retry?

alexa: we can deploy a short-circuit in the edge LB to return 429 for requests with tokens_requested > 400. Doing that for non-SLA.

support-ryan: CS updated customers with current mitigations: fallback routing active, soft throttles in effect, reduced max_tokens, model swapped for some tiers. 

infra-oncall: Good news: queue down to 1.1k, p99=2.9s after model swap + throttles + token cap. Autoscaler still failing on new allocations but pressure is relaxed.

jules: next steps: 1) prepare runbook for when cloud quota is restored — scale back throttles and revert model-swap with canary; 2) create postmortem for quota/auto-scaler interplay and provider api-rate-limit handling; 3) recommend pre-provisioned safety buffer of +10 GPUs for hosted for burst windows.

samir: I'll add a short-term change: autoscaler backoff tuning to avoid provider API rate-limit bursts. And add a circuit-breaker to avoid repeated allocation attempts when quota errors occur.

maria: I'll keep pressure on cloud support for quota increase and update here with ticket id once they reply.

dylan: from customer impact POV: estimated 1.2k requests failed/timeout during the peak window. Affected ~5 large tenants intermittently. Support has list.

support-ryan: confirmed. we've opened tickets for impacted customers and offered credits where SLA breached.

incident-bot: incident declared resolved -> mitigation stable. Root cause: provider GPU quota exhaustion + autoscaler API-rate-triggered provisioning failures leading to queue growth. Severity downgraded to P3 for follow-up work.

jules: I'll own the postmortem and timeline. Assigning action items: infra to add +10 GPU safety buffer and autoscaler backoff (infra-oncall), product to review default token limits and prompt patterns (dylan), support to complete customer outreach (support-ryan), ops to track cloud quota increase (maria).

alexa: thanks all. good coordination. We'll keep this thread open until quota resolved. :white_check_mark:
